title: Defeats for Davi Alcolumbre's Allies in State Elections
seoTitle: Davi Alcolumbre's Allies Face Defeats in State Elections
subtitle: The Senate President sees his allies lose key positions in the 2026 elections
excerpt: In the 2026 elections, the Amapá governor and a Senator allied with Davi Alcolumbre were defeated, causing wear and tear for the Senate President and influencing his.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
In the 2026 state elections, Senate President Davi Alcolumbre (União Brasil-AP) saw his main allies lose their disputes in Amapá. The result alters the political scenario he seeks for re-election to the presidency of the House in 2030.

Defeat of the Governor and Allied Senator

With 92.79% of the ballots counted, Governor Clécio Luís (União Brasil) was defeated in the first round by former mayor Dr. Furlan (PSD), who secured 62.25% of the votes against the incumbent's 37.47%. In the same election, Senator Randolfe Rodrigues (PT), an ally of Alcolumbre and a candidate for re-election, was also ousted, placing third with 18.79%.

Consequences for Alcolumbre's Re-election Strategy

Alcolumbre did not run for office in 2026 but is monitoring the performance of his political group. The defeats weaken his support base in the state and increase pressure on his candidacy for the Senate's Presiding Board, scheduled for February 2027, and his eventual re-election in 2030.

Alcolumbre's Reaction to the Result

In an official statement, Alcolumbre affirmed that he received the result "with respect" and that his defense of the state "remains." The text emphasizes the need for serenity to recognize the popular will and the responsibility to continue working for development, security, and opportunities for Amapá.

Relationship with the President of the Republic

After the Senate's historic defeat to President Lula in another vote, Alcolumbre resumed dialogue with the government. He participated in an agenda with Lula in Amapá to announce the discovery of oil at the mouth of the Amazon and announced that the Senate will vote on the PEC (Proposed Constitutional Amendment) that ends the 6x1 workweek, a measure seen as support for the president.

Impact on Public Perceptions

The electoral losses create wear and tear for Alcolumbre, who already faces public image rejection. The weakening of his political group in Amapá could influence the composition of the Senate's Presiding Board and the support negotiations between the Legislative and Executive branches in the coming years.

With information from O GLOBO.
